recommendations.text: Recommendations to the competent authority of Bulgaria It is recommended that: · the pace of identification of livestock be accelerated; · draft legislation including animal welfare be implemented as soon as possible; 8 · that the veterinary services ensure adequate record keeping in the Central Veterinary Laboratory for Exotic Diseases; · the veterinary services ensure, before proposing milk plants producing sheep cheese for approval of import into the European Union, that structural problems be solved, a HACCP programme be implemented and that the raw material be grade A sheep milk only; · the veterinary services either suspend import of meat into the European Union from one slaughterhouse, where deficiencies have been identified, until it is brought up to standard, or delist it. A report on the actions taken should be submitted to the services of the European Commission within one month.

Recommendations to the services of the European Commission It is recommended: · to lift the restrictions on the imports of bovine, ovine and caprine animals into the European Union from certain banned regions in Bulgaria, except from the 20 km border zone with Turkey, provided that the animals are subjected to a quarantine period of 15 days under official supervision prior to the import into the European Union; · to lift the restrictions on the imports of bovine and sheep meat into the European Union from certain banned regions in Bulgaria, except from the 20 km border zone with Turkey. 9

Take urgent action to rectify the deficiencies found during the mission. Special attention must be paid to improving the slaughter hygiene and to increase the veterinary supervision at the local and regional level (see 5.6.4.). It is advisable to distinguish inspection/veterinary personnel in the slaughterhouses (service badges, helmets of different colour, etc.) as well as the inspection points. It is also advisable to establish a systematic approach to water sampling and examination in approved establishments. A report indicating the completed correction measures, which have been verified by the CA, should be submitted to the Commission within two months of receiving this report.

Take action to fully implement the animal identification system in sheep. A report indicating schedule of measures to be taken, including deadlines should be submitted to the Commission within two months of receiving this report.

Take action to fully implement the HACCP system and improve the own checks in all establishments, and to provide official staff with appropriate training. A report indicating schedule of measures to be taken, including deadlines should be submitted to the Commission within two months of receiving this report. 12 7.2. To the European Commission Services After receiving satisfactory guarantees in respect of paragraphs 7.1.1. and 7.1.3. from the Bulgarian CA: 7.2.1. Consider approval of a meat processing plant for export into the Community. 7.2.2. Consider approval of three milk processing establishments producing milk- based products for export into the community. 7.2.3. Consider maintaining on the list two approved slaughterhouses and the one combined slaughterhouse and cutting plant currently listed.
It is recommended to improve the training of the official veterinarians in the district veterinary services and to reinforce the supervision of the service at this level.

Transpose the full equivalent of the EU legislation with relation to the monitoring plan and in particular the Council Regulation 2377/90 and the Council Directive 90/676/EC. Page 14 of 17 DG(SANCO)/1037-2000 - final
Take the necessary corrective measures regarding the residue monitoring plan in the light of the deficiencies identified by the mission team.

The identification system should be improved in order to assure traceability of animals and carcasses back to the farm. Install a register at the farms allowing the official veterinarians to make the necessary verifications before signing a health certificate for the animals.
Provide the official veterinarians with instructions concerning targeted sampling and suspected cases.

Reinforce the supervision of the distribution of medicines which can be used in the veterinary field in order to guarantee a correct implementation of the Bulgarian legislation and in particular take the appropriate measures that stilbenes are not used in food producing animals. Start collaboration with all the involved services in order to have an overall supervision of the whole production, import and export of all medicines available in the country.

Establish a training programme for the laboratory staff and ameliorate the access to scientific literature. Improve the analytical performance of the laboratory and establish a quality control according to international recognised standards within the analytical measurements, in particular for the validation of the methods. Taking into account the significant findings mentioned above the inadequate supervision of distribution of medicines as well as the unreliable results of analysis in the laboratory, the Bulgarian competent authority should forward to the European Commission written guarantees about rectifying all the points listed above. In particular, points 6 and 7 should be addressed immediately, and corresponding measures presented in the comments which are due into 10 working days after receiving this draft report. Detailed information on (a) whatever action has been and will be taken and (b) the deadlines by which this action has been or will be completed should be provided to the European Commission every month to be able to follow up the progress achieved in correcting the deficiencies. 7.2. To the Commission Services After having received the guarantees of the competent authority, a follow-up mission should be organised in the short term in order to verify the effectiveness of the guarantees and to re-assess the competent authorities, in terms of the control of residues in live animals and products of animal origin. If the deficiencies were not corrected, the Commission should seriously consider recommending the prohibition of imports of Bulgarian products of animal origin to the EU. Concerning the corrective actions, the following information has been transmitted to the European Commissio 1 It was stated that the General Directorate of the NVS will prepare a training course for the authorised veterinarians before the 30th of June 2000. No statement has been made yet with regard to the reinforcement of the supervision of the district veterinary services. Recommendation 2 To bring the requested equivalent legislation into force, deadlines were proposed by the competent authority for the transposition of EU legislation Council Directives 96/22 and 96/23 and Council Regulation 2377/90, but not for the Council Directive 90/676. Recommendation 3 The residue monitoring plan for 2000 and the results for 1999 have been received by the Commission. Antithyriod substances have been included in the plan for 2000, but the method of analysis is not yet developed. Recommendation 4 It was stated that an update of Ordinance No 3 concerning import of live big and small ruminants and the meat from them, will be elaborated by 30th of June 2000. It will include several items such as animal identification and registration of medical treatment. The withdrawal period for medical treatment will be recorded in an ambulant register book, kept at the veterinary units. No information has been given yet concerning the improvement of the identification system to assure traceability of animals and carcasses back to the farm. Recommendation 5 It was stated that instructions will be drawn up for targetted sampling and suspected cases before 30th June 2000. Recommendation 6 The supervision on the distribution, sale and usage of veterinary medicines will be strengthened as well as the supervision of the veterinary pharmacies. In the invoices, sent from manufacturers of veterinary medicines to wholesalers, additional information will have to be included. With the Executive Agency for medicinal products, a Memorandum of understanding has been drawn up. Also a program for the supervision of the production and trade of veterinary medicines has been elaborated. Page 16 of 17 DG(SANCO)/1037-2000 - fi 7 Training of the laboratory staff and improvement of the analytical capacities has been foreseen in the two year Twinning Project BG 9806-03-01. Ten Bulgarian laboratory experts participated in training in Italy concerning ISO norms and EN 45001. No information is given concerning the missing validation documentation of the methods used in the National Reference Laboratory. Page 17 of 17

Shortcomings and deficiencies to improve the Bulgarian food control and monitoring system The Competent Authorities should address the shortcomings and deficiencies, stated above under points 5 and 6 of this report, in order to improve the official control system of foodstuffs intended for export into the EU. 14

Method of sampling of mushroom consignments intended for export into the EU Comprehensive written procedures should be developed to ensure that sampling of mushrooms from consignments intended for export into the EU is a planned procedure of collection to yield a representative sample as required in Annex II to Commission Regulation (EC) No 1661/1999.

Obtaining export certificates for mushroom consignments intended for export into the EU Inspectors of the regional or sub-regional Services for Plant Protection, Quarantine and Agrochemistry should ensure that the consignments described in the export certificates are the actual consignments from which samples were taken and are within specified accumulated radioactivity levels.

The bluetongue serological situation should continue to be monitored. Any further vaccination should contain only those serotypes which have been identified in Bulgaria and neighbouring countries.

The surveillance/control of CSF in wild and semi-wild pigs should be improved so that an eradication policy can be adopted, thus eliminating the need for compulsory vaccination. In the meantime, improved supervision is necessary over small pig holdings.

At the CVRI the accuracy, clarity and presentation of the laboratory management and recording systems should be improved as a matter of urgency. The administrative restructuring of the laboratory should take place as soon as possible with a view to seeking accreditation.

Record keeping at the regional and local level should be more transparent, recorded in a standard way and filed logically so information can be located quickly. A system should be introduced to allow the CA in Sofia to obtain an up-to-date overview of activities/results in all the regions.

Identification of small ruminants and registration of holdings should be put in place for the whole country as soon as possible and should include suitable ear-tags, registers and a central database. 16 A plan describing the actions to be taken and the deadlines by which they will be completed should be submitted to the Commission within two months of receipt of the final report. 9. ADDENDUM TO THE MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO) 1186/2000 In their comments to the draft report the Bulgarian authority has responded to each of the recommendations at point 8.1. of the draft report indicating the action to be undertaken. Specific time frames and defined deadlines for the completion of some of these actions are given for recommendations 8.1.3, 8.1.4 and 8.1.5. With regards to recommendation 8.1.2 the CA states that the action has already been completed. In response to recommendation 8.1.1 the authority stated that no vaccination against bluetongue is likely to be carried out in 2001. 17

As regards public health the competent authorities of Bulgaria should take the following actions: 20 ­ the shortcomings noted in the plants visited, and shortcomings of similar type in all the other EC approved establishments, should be rectified, ­ the own checks in the EC approved establishments should be reviewed in order to assure that they are properly focussed and all the procedures are sufficiently documented. ­ potable water used in the EC approved establishments should be tested more frequently in order to verify the compliance with the microbiological parameters laid down in the EC legislation.
As regards certification, the competent authorities of Bulgaria should issue only uniquely numbered certificates based on models laid down in the EC legislation.
As regards animal welfare, the competent authorities of Bulgaria should ensure that the deficiencies in stunning and its supervision are urgently rectified.

As regards animal health, and in particular to fulfil the EC requirements for live poultry exports, the competent authorities of Bulgaria should take the following actions: ­ the national legislation concerning Newcastle disease should be urgently amended to bring it into compliance with the EC legislation and it should be implemented without delay, ­ the role of the poultry department of the CVMRI as the national reference laboratory for Newcastle disease and avian influenza should be properly defined, and ­ the tasks and responsibilities of the official diagnostic laboratories for diagnoses of poultry diseases, in particular of Newcastle disease and avian influenza, should be clearly defined and their approval and supervision properly organised.

The competent authorities of Bulgaria should inform the Commission of the progress with and results of the measures taken, within three months following the receipt of the final report, including a timetable for completion of measures and actions still outstanding at that time. 6.2. Recommendations to the Commission services Provided the competent authorities of Bulgaria have supplied the necessary satisfactory guarantees with regards to the issues mentioned under point 6.1, fourth paragraph, the Commission Services should consider approving Bulgaria for imports of live poultry. 21 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)1200/2000 Competent Authority's (CA) response to the recommendations in the report The CA has stated, in their fax of 8 February 2001, that the following actions have been or will be taken to rectify the shortcomings indicated during the FVO inspection: · The NVS headquarters have informed the relevant regional veterinary services and the management of the EC approved poultry slaughterhouses of the deficiencies found during the FVO inspection. The establishments have been instructed to rectify the relevant shortcomings under the supervision of the veterinary services. · The regional veterinary services have been ordered to ensure that deficiencies in stunning are corrected and its supervision properly documented. · Potable water used in the EC approved establishments will be tested four times per year for microbiological parameters laid down in the Community legislation. · The draft ordinance on control of Newcastle disease complying with the Community legislation will come into force in March 2001. The national contingency plan for Newcastle disease will take effect simultaneously. · The CVMRI has been directly subordinated to the NVS and its role as a national reference laboratory for Newcastle disease and avian influenza confirmed. The CVMRI will establish professional contacts with the Community reference laboratory. 22
To ensure that all wild game meat exported from Bulgaria to the EU complies with the provisions of Council Directive 92/45/EEC. Page 14 of 15
To correct the deficiencies identified at the establishments visited, and to ensure that all game processing premises comply with the requirements of the relevant EU legislation.
To take the necessary action to ensure that official veterinarians fully understand the health certification.

To adopt Council Directive 92/45/EEC into the Bulgarian veterinary legislation as soon as possible and initiate the necessary staff training. The authorities of Bulgaria should prepare an action plan to address both the above general recommendations, and the detailed conclusions of this report. This plan should indicate the deadlines for the implementation and completion of each of the actions. The plan should be submitted to the Commission's services within three months of receipt of the final report. 8.2. To the Commission Services 8.2.1. Subject to the receipt of satisfactory guarantees from the Central Competent Authority, within the deadlines given in the mission report, the Commission Services should retain Bulgaria on the list of third countries approved for export of wild game meat to the EU. 9. ADDENDUM The Bulgarian authorities offered comments on the draft report by means of a letter dated 25 January 2001. They gave a preliminary indication of the action taken in response to parts of the report, and undertook to provide details of the measures taken to address the outstanding issues identified in the report. Legislation The NVS should take all necessary action to harmonise the legislation relating to the purpose of the mission with EU legislation and to implement it for products intended for export to the EU.

Laboratories The NVS should take the necessary measures to improve the standard of its laboratories, and to ensure that analyses of fish, fishery products and drinking water are performed in accordance with EU requirements or international standards.
Residue monitoring plan The annual residue monitoring plan should be drawn up and implemented taking into account the shortcomings mentioned in the report.

Veterinary supervision The NVS should take strict measures to ensure the correct issue of export health certificates by veterinary inspectors. In particular, the shortcomings regarding export certification of caviar should be investigated. Furthermore, the NVS should address all the deficiencies mentioned in the report. Further training of veterinary inspectors to enhance their competence in hygiene and certification procedures should be undertaken.

Written guarantees The Bulgarian competent authority should forward to the European Commission written guarantees in respect of the rectification of all the points listed above, and provide detailed information on the action that has been and will be taken and on the deadlines by which this action has been or will be completed. 2 Written guarantees concerning improvements to be made in the SISVSC (PH) laboratory. 25 8.2. To the Commission services ­ The Commission services should evaluate the written assurances received from the Bulgarian competent authority. ­ Provided that these guarantees are satisfactory, the Commission services should propose that Bulgaria be placed on list I in the Annex to the amended Commission Decision 97/296/EC and that a Commission Decision laying down the health conditions for the importation of fishery products originating in Bulgaria be adopted. The list of approved establishments should be limited to the list proposed at the time of the mission and any extension of the list should be subject to a follow-up mission. 26 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/3335/2001 Competent Authority response to the recommendations in the report The Bulgarian competent authority has provided comments on the report, which will be published together with the final report on the website of the Health and Consumer Protection Directorate-General. In its comments, the competent authority provided assurances in respect of most of the recommendations contained in the report, and in particular: - Draft legislation has been prepared to rectify the shortcomings noted during the mission; - Order No RD 09-778, adopted on 16 July 2001, bans the use of chloramphenicol for injection or oral administering in food-producing animals; - Order No XI-195, adopted on 28 August 2001 establishes that, in the plants proposed for export to the EU, samples of fishery products and drinking water should only be sent for analysis to the three accredited laboratories mentioned in the comments; - Measures have been taken in order to upgrade the Laboratory at the Sofia Inspectorate of State Veterinary Sanitary Control (Public Health), the Central Laboratory for Veterinary Sanitary Expertise and Ecology and the Laboratory for Fish Diseases in Sofia. Improvement to their quality system and validation of analysis methods are ongoing; - The national residue monitoring programme will be amended for year 2002 in order to include sampling of other aquaculture species than carp, silver carp and trout. The Burgas region will be included in the programme for the second half of 2001, in order to check the presence of chlorine-organic compounds; - Training of veterinary inspectors on certification procedures was carried out on 20 July 2001 (public health certificates) and 24 July 2001 (animal health certificates); - Measures have been taken or ordered to address the deficiencies noted in the four fishery product establishments visited. 27

audits.title: Export of animals and animal products to the EU

recommendations.text: To continue current actions to transpose and implement EU legislative requirements.
To ensure that certification for exports to the EU is prepared and issued fully in accordance with EU requirements.
To ensure that animal disease monitoring programmes are fully and effectively implemented, and to maintain a high state of vigilance for exotic diseases.

To take all necessary action to ensure that EU approved food processing establishments fully comply with EU requirements. A plan describing the actions to be taken to address the above recommendations, and providing deadlines by which they will be completed, should be submitted to the Commission within three months of receipt of the final report. 11. ADDENDUM The Bulgarian authorities commented on the draft report in a fax, dated 21 February 2002. In light of these comments, some further clarifications have been included as footnotes to the report. They also provided further information on the action taken in respect of the non-compliant premises (see point 8), and of certain other issues identified in the report. 18
Veterinary supervision The CCA should address all the deficiencies mentioned in the report. Special attention is required to address the non-compliances concerning labelling and certification.

Legislation Where the Bulgarian legislation does not cover specific Community legal provisions, guarantees should be provided to the Commission services that fishery products exported to the EU meet equivalent requirements to the relevant Community legislation.

Laboratories The CCA should take the necessary measures to improve the standard of its laboratories, and to ensure that analyses of fish and fishery products are performed in accordance with standards at least equivalent to those of the Community requirements or equivalent to international standards. Inter- calibration tests should be organised and carried out with all laboratories involved in the testing of fish and fishery products.

Residue monitoring plan (a) The CCA should consider to include in the residue monitoring plan for aquaculture products tests to detect the presence of other nitrofurans, in addition to what is currently checked (Furazolidone). (b) The CCA should include heavy metals and organochlorinated substances in the monitoring of environmental contaminants in wild fish, such as sturgeon, pike and pike perch.

Written guarantees The CCA should forward to the Commission services written guarantees in respect of all the points listed above within 25 working days after receipt of the draft report, including an action plan in which a detailed timetable for all the necessary corrective actions is drawn up. 5.2. To the Commission services Provided that adequate action is taken and detailed guarantees are received from the Bulgarian CA, modification of Commission Decision 2002/472/EC and its Annexes (establishments and model health certificate) could be considered. 10 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT SANCO/9287/2003 The CA of Bulgaria informed the Commission services via e-mail on 1 April 2004 of the progress and the result of the measures taken after the mission. Related to the Veterinary supervision: A training session was carried out in January 2004 in order to address the deficiencies identified by the mission team. The NVS has addressed the follow-up in two establishments where deficiencies were found during the mission. As part of the same communication, the CA forwarded to the FVO services guarantees issued by the Central Laboratory in Sofia and the Regional Veterinary Service in Vidin related to the Residue Monitoring Plan, and guarantees issued by the Regional Veterinary Services in Smolyan and Vidin related to the accreditation and standardisation of the methods in the Regional Laboratories.
Fully transpose Articles 2 and 6 of Council Directive 93/85/EEC specifying testing for latent infection in the general surveys and of potatoes clonally related to contaminated lots;
Ensure that in the national seed potato certification legislation there is zero tolerance for all the quarantine pests and diseases listed in the community legislation;
Include in the national surveys for ring rot and R. solanacearum a representative sample of the non-registered small producer sector;

Ensure that systematic investigations of clonal or other links are carried out in case of a ring rot or brown rot outbreak and that probable contamination is designated and a quarantine zone demarcated accordingly. Improvement of the existing contingency plans with these points could be helpful;
Adopt the revised EU official test methods for C. michiganensis ssp. sepedonicus and R. solanacearum as soon as these have been published;
Consider improving the quality control at the RPPSs through the use of regular blind positive and negative control samples;

Report to the European Commission concerning the potato wart disease outbreak on: a. Final details of the measures taken on the contaminated plots and surrounding area, b. Outcome of the 2005 follow-up survey, c. Outcome of the pathotype investigations;
Immediately notify the European Commission of any outbreaks of potato ring rot or R. solanacearum or other significant outbreaks of potato quarantine pests or diseases;
Finalise the registration of entities (producers, dispatching centres, collective warehouses) that market ware potatoes;

Replace, before accession to the EU, the requirement for plant passports for ware potatoes with the labelling requirements, mentioned in Council Directive 2000/29/EC, Annex IV, part A, section II, point 18.5. Bulgaria is requested to report to the Commission, within two months following receipt of the final report, on any action taken and/or planned in response to the recommendations. The deadline for completion of any planned measures should be indicated. 15 10. ADDENDUM Bulgaria has given an initial response to the recommendations as follows: Re. 1. The mentioned articles shall be fully transposed with the forthcoming amendments in the legislation and no later than six months prior to the accession. Re. 2. The NPPS is committed to implement this by the end of 2005 at the latest. Re 3. Within the 2005 plan for phytosanitary control of ware potatoes, representative samples of non-registered small producers are included. This will continue also in the future annual national surveys. Re 4. These objectives were already included in the preliminary strategy for the control of these diseases. Re 5. The NPPS will adopt the new test procedures right away after their publishing. Re 6. The introduction of control samples is foreseen in the 2005 plan. Re 7. The NPPS will report to the Commission on the wart disease outbreak by the end of 2005 at the latest. Re 8. The NPPS will immediately inform the European Commission of any outbreaks. Re 9. The registration continues. Re 10. The NPPS will replace the requirement for plant passports for ware potatoes through the relevant amendments of the legislation at the latest six months before accession 16

The CA should continue their efforts to work in accordance with Community rules. In particular, where incomplete or incorrect transposition of the Community Acquis in the veterinary field occurs, they should amend the legal texts adopted so far, e.g. to include ratites in the definition of poultry in Ordnance 47/2002.

The CA should provide the NRL with the necessary resources to ensure swift testing of samples submitted and to allow it to work in accordance with Quality Assurance standards. In particular, the traceability of samples within the NRL should be improved.

The CCA should pay attention to the harmonisation and standardisation of the regional CPs, in order to facilitate their operability in particular when staff from outside the relevant RVS is temporarily employed in the event of an emergency. In order to facilitate the supervision on the regional CPs, it is also recommended that their different versions should be dated.
The CCA should provide the relevant service of the NVS with the necessary resources to operate a fully fledged NCC. The procedures for the activation of this centre should be clearly defined.
The CCA should continue its efforts regarding training and include certain aspects of large scale culling of poultry.
Recording of the sampling and of the progress of surveys should be improved.

The CCA should consider whether other means can be used than fines to enforce veterinary legislation in back-yard flocks when there is a risk of introduction or spread of contagious animal diseases. In particular, the possibility to confiscate and destroy animals or goods which pose a potential threat should be considered.

Ensure that inspectors with responsibility for carrying out food hygiene inspections receive adequate training as required by Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. This is particularly important with reference to the assessment of HACCP principles (Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004) and of general food hygiene requirements (Annex II of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004) as required by Article 10(2) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Finalise measures for national contingency plan as required by Article 13 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

Ensure that official controls include the assessment of HACCP principles (Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004) and of general food hygiene requirements (Annex II of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004) as required by Article 10(2) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Ensure that official control samples are taken in accordance with Article 11 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Ensure that the requirements for food allergen labelling (Article 6 of Directive 2000/13/EC) are enforced in accordance with Article 10 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

Ensure that only laboratories which comply with Article 12 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004, or at least with the derogation under Article 18 of Regulation (EC) No 2076/2005, are designated to carry out analysis of samples taken during official control. 19 An action plan in response to the recommendations should be forwarded to the Commission within 25 days of receipt of the report. This action plan should clearly set out the manner and deadline by which the competent authorities will address each of the above recommendations. 9. COMPETENT AUTHORITY RESPONSE TO RECOMMENDATIONS

audits.title: Controls on Feed and compliance with requirements for Feed Hygiene

recommendations.text: To ensure that feed inspectors are responsible for verification of the implementation of requirements on HACCP procedures and quality control, as laid down in Art. 6 of Regulation 183/2005 and its Annex II respectively, are trained to undertake their duties competently, as required by Art. 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To ensure that the annual control plan for inspections of FBOs and sampling of feed takes into account the reliability of FBO own checks as required by Art. 3.1 (c) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To designate laboratories able to carry out the analyses of all samples taken during official controls on feed, as required by Art. 12 of Regulation (EC) no 882/2004.
To designate a NRL for feed additives as required by Art. 33 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To continue the process of registration primary producers of feed as required by Art. 9 of Regulation (EC) No 183/2005.
To take steps to ensure that the HACCP procedures laid down by Art. 6 of Regulation (EC) No 183/2005 are implemented.

To authorise imports only under the conditions laid down in Art. 6 of Directive 98/51/EC, establishing a list of representatives in the EU of establishments located in third countries and requiring a declaration of compliance with EU requirements for feed hygiene. 8. To transpose Directive 98/68/EC. 9. To reinforce the sampling programme aimed at ensuring compliance with the phasing out of antibiotics as feed additives laid down by Art. 11 of Regulation (EC) No 1831/2004. 10. To provide administrative assistance to the authorities in other MSs, as required by Art. 34(2) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004, concerning the dispatch into their territory of additives (for export) that cannot be used within the EU according to Art. 11 of Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003. 14 DG(SANCO)/7272/2007 ­ MR Final 11. To reinforce compliance with the rules on dioxins laid down by Directive 2002/32/EC on undesirable substances in order to ensure that the maximum levels set out in Annex II are not exceeded. 12. To transpose Directives 2006/13/C and 2006/77/C. __________________ COMPETENT AUTHORITY RESPONSE TO RECOMMENDATIONS

To ensure that the National Control Disease Centre and Expert Groups are established and operate in accordance with Article 23 of Council Directive 2001/89/EC, in particular to define and revise the necessary control measures, to deploy the necessary staff and resources, to ensure adequate epidemiological enquiries and to liaise with diagnostic laboratory.
To ensure that adequate laboratory capacity is available for the control of CSF, as required by Article 4, 2, c of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To ensure that the interpretation of results of laboratory tests are performed and validated in accordance with the Diagnostic Manual.

To put in place a quality control scheme ensuring that sampling, testing and and interpretation of results are performed according to Good Laboratory Practices, 18 quality and traceability standards described in Article 12, 2 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To ensure that the CA has legal power and properly enforces provisions for holding registration, animal identification, movement controls and compulsory notification of diseases;

To ensure that conditions foreseen for the establishment of PZs and SZs, and the measures (Articles 9, 10 and 11 of Council Directive 2001/89/EC) are properly applied, and to ensure that restriction measures are not lifted before the absence of virus circulation is assured.

To ensure that disinfection is performed with approved disinfectants and according to comprehensive guidelines, as required by Article 12 of Council Directive 2001/89/EC, and to ensure its effective implementation by adequate controls and verification procedures, as required by Article 8 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To develop the control of the vaccination programme, and the specific assessment of the plan for the eradication of CSF in feral pigs and the control and monitoring programme of CSF, in order to validate their effective and efficient application, in accordance with Commission Decisions 2006/800/EC and 2006/876/EC.
To improve the use of the eradication plan to prevent virus circulation in the event of detection of CSF in feral pigs, in accordance with Article 16 of Council Directive 2001/89/EC.

To ensure a strict application of measures foreseen in Article 10, 1, f, Article 10, 3, f, and Article 11, 1 f of Council Directive 2001/89/EC, for the pigs transported from a PZ or SZ to a slaughterhouse; to ensure that meat of pigs slaughtered after the probable introduction of disease in the holding is traced in accordance with Article 5, 1, d of the same Directive.

To guarantee that pig meat and meat products are dispatched to other Member States only when a reinforced, reliable, and auditable control system is operational to ensure the respect of the requirements of Commission Decision 2006/805/EC. 9. COMPETENT AUTHORITY RESPONSE TO RECOMMENDATIONS

audits.title: Import/transit control system and border inspection posts

recommendations.text: To establish a procedure so that overlapping of responsibilities is avoided and coordination within the CAs is strengthened according to Art. 4 (5) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. To take the necessary steps to ensure that the conditions of approval of warehouses are maintained (Art. 12.5 of Directive 97/78/EC) and that warehouses are under the control of the CA (Art. 3 of Decision 2000/571/EC).

To improve co-operation of BIPs with Customs and to ensure access of BIP staff to relevant information in customs information systems as required by Artt. 6 and 7 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004 and Artt. 5 and 6 of Regulation (EC) No 282/2004. Additionally, to ensure that Customs do not allow entrance of consignments in free zones without veterinary authorisation according to Art. 24 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To take measures to ensure that CITES live animals and POAO only enter through points with a suitable approved BIP in order to comply with Artt. 3 of Directives 97/78/EC and 91/496/EEC.

To ensure that all staff involved in official controls receive appropriate training, records are kept and staff is up-to-date in their areas of competence as required in Art. 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 and Annex to Decision 2001/812/EC.

To ensure that the records of results of checks in free zones and customs warehouses are available at the BIPs in accordance with paragraphs 4 and 5 of Annex to Decision 2001/812/EC. To ensure that IATA rules are available to the relevant BIPs according to paragraph 3 of Annex to Decision 2001/812/EC.
To ensure that the annual monitoring sampling plan is based upon the nature of the products and the risk they represent in accordance with point 1 of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 136/2004.

To complete instructions to BIPs such as for laboratory checks, animal health requirements for consignments in transit and further clarify for BIP staff the reimport procedure according to Art. 8 (1) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To implement internal or external audits as provided for in Art. 4 (6) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 and improve the supervisory system and the relevant check-lists for the verification procedures in order to ensure that any specific shortcomings are detected and timely corrected as required in Art. 8 (3) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To ensure that satisfactory action is taken for the correction of shortcomings for the poor conditions of working hygiene and maintenance of the BIPs according to Annex II of Directive 97/78/EC and Annex A of Directive 91/496/EEC.

To consider application of sanctions in order to provide a sufficient deterrent in order to improve notification in advance of arrival of consignments as required by Artt. 54 and 55 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To complete the MANCP with the official import/transit controls according to Artt. 41 and 42 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To ensure transparency for official import/transit controls by making available the relevant information on the control activities to the public according to Art. 7 (1) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To establish a list of approved channelled establishments according to Art. 8 (6) of Directive 97/78/EC.
To ensure that fees are collected at EU minimum level according to Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To take measures to ensure entry of correct information in TRACES in order to comply with the requirements of Art. 3 (3) of Commission Decision 2004/292/EC.

To ensure that all consignments for import and transit are presented directly to BIPs in order to undergo the required veterinary checks according to Artt. 3 of Directives 97/78/EC and 91/496/EEC and that storage in warehouses beforehand does not take place.

To ensure that there is a link in customs systems for the transited consignments (such as NCTS) with the positive list under the Decision 2007/275/EC in order to better implement Art. 3 to Directive 97/78/EC.

To ensure that the procedures for veterinary checks (especially documentary checks) and decision on consignment, including transit, the re-import procedure and the procedure for rejection and re-dispatched are followed in accordance with Directives 97/78/EC and 91/496/EEC.
To ensure that no live animals are accepted for exit transit through BIPs without having the appropriate approval category according to Artt. 4, 6 and 9 of Directive 91/496/EEC .

To ensure that a procedure is in place for detained consignments to be kept under veterinary control in an appropriate storage as laid down in Art. 4 (3) of Decision 2001/812/EC, in Art. 17 of Directive 97/78/EC and Art. 18 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To ensure that BIPs comply with the applicable requirements concerning working hygiene, facilities, maintenance and equipment according to Decision 2001/812/EEC and Directive 91/496/EEC. To establish a system that ensures adequate control, working hygiene, equipment and maintenance of facilities for all BIPs in order to ensure ongoing compliance with the provisions of Decision 2001/812/EC and Directive 91/496/EEC.

To consider to adopt a procedure for suspension of BIPs in order to ensure that in case of public or animal health risk the relevant approval may be suspended as required by Art. 6 of Directive 97/78/EC.
To take measures to correct all minor short comings for facilities, equipment, hygiene and procedures in all BIPs in order to comply with the provisions of Decision 2001/812/EC.

To take measures to correct the significant shortcomings in the facilities, equipment and working hygiene in Kapitan Andreevo BIP in order to comply with the provisions of Decision 2001/812/EC including the approval for NHC-T(CH) and NHC-T(FR) for which the BIP is not compliant.

audits.title: Import controls on food of plant origin

recommendations.text: Ensure efficient and effective cooperation between the CAs in relation to import controls of food of non-animal origin as required by Article 4(3) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

Continue with the training of staff performing import controls of FNAO, in particular laboratory staff, to ensure that they receive appropriate training for their area of competence, as established in Article 6 and Annex II of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Ensure that the procedure used for mycotoxins sampling is updated as required by Article 8(3)(b) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

Ensure that all methods used by laboratories designated for import controls of FNAO, are validated and they are included in the scope of accreditation as required by Article 12 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

Ensure that the information on all CPs authorised under the Article 19 of Regulation (EC) No 669/2009 is transparent enough to identify them clearly as required by Article 7 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Ensure that audits are carried out in the units of the MH responsible for import controls as required by Article 4(6) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Ensure that the MANCP contains all the information required in Article 42(2)(e) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Ensure that all control points are adequately authorised by the CA for the purpose of carrying out identity and physical checks as provided for in Article 19 of Regulation (EC) No 669/2009.
Ensure that the prior notification procedure is followed by FBOs at the Kapitan Andreevo DPE as required by Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 669/2009.
Ensure that, when the consignments are bound for identity and physical checks at the CPs, these checks are always carried out as required by Article 8 (1) (b) of Regulation (EC) No 669/2009.
Ensure that the sampling frequency complies with Annex I of Regulation (EC) No 669/2009.
Ensure that documentary checks are properly carried out in accordance with Article 7 of Regulation (EC) No 1152/2009.

Ensure that, when the CA allows for the onward transportation to the other MS, the CA at the DPE notifies the CA at the point of destination and appropriate arrangements are put in place to ensure that the consignment remains under the continuous control of the CAs as required by Article 8(2) of Regulation (EC) No 669/2009.

Ensure that the NRL for mycotoxins in food is clearly designated and both, the NRL for mycotoxins and the NRL for pesticide residues analyses in fruit and vegetables under the MH, carry out all tasks required by Article 33(2) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

Ensure that SANCO Guidelines 10684/2009 on method validation and quality control procedures for pesticide residue analysis in food and feed, adopted on the basis of Article 28(2) of Regulation (EC) No 396/2005, are fully followed, including samples preparation, especially in the case of laboratory performing analyses of amitraz, metomyl and oxamyl in products originating from Turkey.
Ensure that the analytical method used for Sudan Dyes I-IV is validated and is included in the scope of accreditation as required by Article 12 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

Ensure that laboratory performing mycotoxins analyses complies with Annex I point A.3.7 and Annex II point 4.4 of Regulation (EC) No 401/2006, completes validation of the aflatoxins method with studies on accuracy, reproducibility and measurement uncertainty as required by Annex III in Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 and operates fully in accordance with EN ISO/IEC 17025 as required by Article 12(2) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
Ensure that aggregate sample obtained can be considered as representative of the lot, as required by Annex I point A.1 of Regulation (EC) No 401/2006.

responses.response: "Animal Health and Welfare" Directorate (AHWD) has developed by Instruction for performing official controls concerning salmonelloses in poultry, in particular in laying hens, breeding herds, broilers and turkey, this instruction being endorsed and entered into effect by BFSA Order of ref. No RD 11-1063/30.08.2012 signed by BFSA Executive Director. This document lays down in details the obligations of the experts of AHWD at central level, of official veterinarians in the country and of "Animal Health" Department chiefs at Regional Food Safety Directorates (RFSD) concerning the mode or procedures to be applied by them when performing inspections, when collecting and tracing the data for the performance of relevant Salmonelloses control programmes (plans) in respective poultry categories. audits.title: evaluate the national procedures in place to verify the effectiveness of the import control system

recommendations.text: To ensure that the procedures for verification of the official import controls cover the relevant activities of the import control system, ensuring its effectiveness and appropriateness as laid down in Article 4(2)(a) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

citations.text: The new procedure foresees setting of measurable objectives for the official import controls and indicators linked to these objectives, however at the time of the audit the strategic objectives were not developed into operational objectives. The procedure uses the verification of compliance as the basis for verification of effectiveness, and highlights the difference between the two concepts. However both concepts get mixed later in the document.

The objectives of the audit activities on official import controls are to assess the activities and their compliance with the relevant procedures. This includes an evaluation of the appropriateness of the official import controls when a shortcoming in the implementation of these controls is identified. In such a case the audit team is conducting root-cause analysis to determine if the procedure needs to be improved.

The competent authority is developing the activities for verification of effectiveness but has not yet set the relevant indicators to measure the extent to which the objectives are met. Currently the verification activities assess the appropriateness of the official import controls only when a shortcoming in the implementation of the controls is identified.

In both BIPs visited there is cooperation with Customs in respect of Customs nomenclature codes (CN codes) that do not specify the type of commodity. The heads of the BIPs hold regular meetings with Customs officials. A central supervision conducted in October 2013 in both BIPs recommended that these meetings should be documented. These meetings are documented in BIP Gjueshevo but not in BIP Kapetan Andreevo.

The new procedure specifies the measures to ensure that all consignments subject to veterinary checks are identified and presented to the BIP in line with requirements of Article 3 of Directive 97/78/EC and Article 2(1) of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004. The supervision at local level in BIP Kapetan Andreevo assesses the pre-notifications without following the checklist annexed to the new procedure and the relevant instruction for checking a percentage of CVEDs. In BIP Gjueshevo the supervision assesses the pre-notifications following the checklist and relevant instruction.

The heads of both BIPs visited were aware of how the Customs database flags the consignments, but they did not use all intelligence available (Customs documents and data), contrary to the requirement of Article 6 of Regulation 136/2004 to cross check that no import of a consignment violates the requirements of Article 4(1) of Directive 91/496/EEC and Article 3 of Directive 97/78/EC. The verification activities had not identified this shortcoming either at local (supervision) level or at central (supervision, audit) level. 5.2.2 Veterinary checks

The new procedure for the verification of effectiveness has instructions on what percentage of CVEDs should be evaluated. The heads of the BIPs are not following the instruction to select specific amounts of CVEDs to assess performance of official veterinarians. The supervisors stated that they fill the supervision checklist using the previous knowledge they have on each veterinarian's performance.

The local supervision focuses on the performance of the official veterinarians. Having no overview of the official import controls, the supervision does not detect errors by the persons responsible for the loads (pre-notification) or other BIPs and local veterinary units (LVUs) (related to follow-up of the consignments).

The audit team discussed with the competent authority several shortcomings that were not identified by the verification activities of the competent authority (see also finding 27): · First page of CVEDs not complete, or incorrect but were accepted (e.g. Article 12 warehouse accepted CVED from Burgas with an incorrect approval number), contrary to the requirements 2(e) and (h) of Annex 1 to Regulation (EC) No 136/2004 · BIP Bregovo issued CVED for a Customs warehouse, not approved under Article 12 that led to a wrong documentary check and a wrong decision contrary to the requirements of Article 13(1) of Directive 97/78/EC · In BIP Gjueshevo the officials do not unload the consignments for a physical check, contrary to the requirement of Annex III to Directive 97/78/EC. In addition, samples for laboratory testing are taken without unloading the consignment, therefore the sample is not representative of the load contrary to the requirements of Annex III to Directive 97/78/EC. The new procedure for verification of effectiveness and the checklist annexed to it do not specify the evaluation of this aspect of sampling. · In BIP Kapetan Andreevo, a case in which a consignment of pet animals (dogs) was accepted indicated a physical check in TRACES without checking all animals (one of the animals had a different microchip number than the one indicated in the CVEDA). This is not in compliance with the requirement of Article 4(4) of Directive 97/78/EC. The issue was not identified by the verification activities but notified to DG SANCO by the competent authority from the Member State of destination. 5.2.3 Controls of transit/non-EU complying consignments

Root cause analysis of the internal audit concluded that major shortcomings identified are due to the warehouse being approved and starting activities under Article 12 without ensuring availability of procedures. In addition the knowledge of the official veterinarians on their tasks relating to requirements of import legislation had not been updated. The competent authority stated that since the approval of the warehouse no written instruction was provided to the official veterinarians until the time of the internal audit in November 2013. The internal audit report recommended provision of training and documented procedures to the official veterinarians by the end of February 2014. At the time of the audit the competent authority had not implemented the actions planned to address the recommendations contrary to the requirement of Article 8(3)(b) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. 6

In February 2014 the competent authority conducted an unannounced supervision of the warehouse, using a new checklist that will be incorporated into the procedure referred to in finding 2. In this supervision improvements after the 2013 internal audit were confirmed and some shortcomings were identified. The competent authority stated that the checklist is at a draft stage and under review so that it can be used for both supervision from central and local level. The supervision identified the non-confirmation of exit transit in BIP Kapetan Andreevo. However no recommendation was issued and no action plan was implemented contrary to the requirement of Article 8(3)(b) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 (the head of the BIP was not aware of the issue when this was raised during the audit).

The competent authority does not register in TRACES CVEDs for non-complying consignments intended for other warehouses in different Member States, contrary to the requirement of Article 3(2) of Decision No 2004/292/EC.

A local supervision procedure on the warehouse was launched by the LVU in December 2013. This is not related to the procedure described in findings 2-5. This supervision has not identified major shortcomings. The officials performing the supervision are not kept up-to-date relating to official import control requirements, although this was recommended by a relevant internal audit (finding 23). This reduces the capability to identify shortcomings in the operation of the warehouse. The competent authority performed a reconciliation test for quantities of commodities handled in which they used the information in TRACES. The conclusion was that commodities examined had ensured traceability. However the audit team noted that there were cases of non-complying consignments sent to another Member State without registering of the movement in TRACES. This renders TRACES unable to be used for reconciliation activities.

The audit team identified several shortcomings that were not identified by the verification activities of the competent authorities: · Several cases of exit transit not being confirmed in Kapetan Andreevo, contrary to the requirements of Article 11(2)(d) of Directive No 97/78/EC. · For the warehouse approved under Article 12 of Directive 97/78/EC, at least four different names are mentioned in CVEDs. The address for the warehouse has at least two different addresses. This is not in line with the requirement 2(h) of Annex 1 to Regulation (EC) No 136/2004. · The competent authority accepts CVEDs with wrong warehouse registration numbers (for the same warehouse different registration numbers are used, only one being correct). This is not in line with the requirement 2(e and h) of Annex 1 to Regulation (EC) No 136/2004. · CVEDs accompanying consignments exiting the warehouse, indicated in box 37 details of a destination in a third country. This is incorrect and does not comply with Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 136/2004. · CVEDs issued in the warehouse indicated seal checks. This is not possible in the case of consignments that are imported to the warehouse and then split (issuing subsequent CVEDs) and it is not in line with the requirement of Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 136/2004. 7 Conclusion on the implementation of the verification activities

The verification activities largely ensure compliance, of the official import controls, with legal requirements and planned arrangements. For some areas the identification of non-compliances is limited by (i) incomplete scope of the verification (e.g. sampling activities are not covered), (ii) lack of implementation (e.g. there are no cross-checks with the Customs database), and (iii) limited awareness of responsible staff (e.g. the supervision of the warehouse approved under Art. 12 of Directive 97/78/EC).

The outcome of supervision is used in audit planning. The competent authority stated that supervision results are also used by audit activities to verify effectiveness. No methodology and results of this verification were available at the time of the audit.

The competent authority keeps a report of monitoring the status of corrective action plans for supervision activities. This does not include the verification activities in the Article 12 warehouse. In the case of the audit activities certain actions planned were not implemented within the deadline and not at the time of the audit (finding 23). There was no follow-up by the time of the audit, contrary to the requirement of Article 8(3)(b) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

Regarding finding 22 the competent authority implemented a corrective action that required all carton boxes of non-compliant products to be stamped with the CVED number. This was applied to new arriving consignments but no to the goods already in stock. Four months after the internal audit, significant stock introduced before the audit, had no CVED identification in the carton boxes. The audit team noted that the corrective action was not effective to address the shortcoming and this is contrary to the requirement of Article 8(3)(b) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. 8

Regarding finding 25 although the issue was identified long before the internal audit, it is still outstanding despite communication with DG SANCO and guidance received. In addition the corrective action to the recommendation of the audit report indicated sending a letter to the Member States that receive such consignments in order to obtain the registration number of the destination warehouses. At the time of the audit the issue was not addressed contrary to the requirement of Article 8(3)(b) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

The results of the verification activities are used for planning future audits. Improvements following verification on the official import controls are evident, however there are cases in which the verification activities do not ensure that corrective actions are implemented or that they are adequate.

recommendations.text: Ensure that all requirements in the National laws in force in Bulgaria are fully in line with legally binding European Union acts for organic production and labelling of organic products.

citations.text: Even though the current version of the National Regulation is dated June 2014, it does not incorporate some of the requirements of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008, in force since 1 January 2014. Although it is mentioned in the National Regulation that all EU Regulations are directly applicable, this inaccuracy may cause that CBs to not include in their procedures some of the missing EU requirements, as CBs may use the National Regulation rather than the directly applicable EU legislation as a reference when drafting their procedures. This was noted to be the case by the audit team at the headquarters of one of the CBs, which referred in its procedures to the National Regulation and to Regulation (EC) No 834/2007 only. As a result, the requirement for the minimum 10% of visits carried out unannounced, established in Regulation (EC) No 889/2008, which is missing from the National Regulation, was not taken into account by the CB.

In addition, the National Regulation includes some requirements which are not in line with EU Regulations, such as the delegation to CBs of the power to grant derogations on the renewal of flocks and herds and the possibility to grant derogations on housing conditions and stocking densities, which are already phased out in the EU Regulations since 31 December 2013. Although these derogations had not been granted in recent years, they are not in line with EU Regulations.

Furthermore, some of the measures foreseen in the national sanction catalogue are not in line with the requirements in EU Regulations. Only soft measures are foreseen in the catalogue, even in cases of severe, recurrent non-compliances (see paragraphs 90-92). 3 Conclusions on Relevant National Legislation and Provisions

National laws necessary to implement legally binding European Union acts relevant to this audit have been adopted by the CA. However, the fact that the National Regulation does not incorporate all relevant EU requirements creates confusion when it comes to their implementation by CBs. In addition, some of the EU requirements further developed by the National Regulation are not in line with EU Regulations.

recommendations.text: Ensure that cooperation between the Competent Unit and the Bulgarian Accreditation Service Executive Agency is adequate to guarantee that the Competent Unit may carry out its supervisory activities on CBs according to Article 92(c) of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008 30

citations.text: The Bulgarian Accreditation Service Executive Agency (IABSA), under the Ministry of Economy, Energy and Tourism is the national accreditation body. The IABSA is responsible for the accreditation of CBs according to the International Organisation for standardization guide ISO/IEC 17065:20121. At the time of the DG Health and Food 1 The ISO/IEC 17065:2012-Conformity assessment- Requirements for bodies certifying products, processes and services, was published in September 2012 and replaced ISO Guide 65 and EN 45011. In accordance with an 4 Safety audit, all the CBs operating in Bulgaria were already accredited to ISO/IEC 17065, having completed the transition from previous standards before September 2015. As regards the exchange of information with the CU on the results of the accreditation audits carried out on CBs, the audit team noted that the CU requested this information on 23 June 2014 but at the time of the audit it had not been provided by the IABSA. This lack of cooperation prevents the CU from effectively carrying out its supervisory activities on CBs according to Article 92(c) of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008 (see paragraph 17).

CAs are designated in Bulgaria with a clear division of responsibilities and tasks. However, cooperation between the CU and the IABSA is not adequate to ensure that the CU fulfils its supervisory activities on CBs.

recommendations.text: Ensure that information on the results of inspections and visits are adequately communicated to the National Paying Agency, as required by Article 92(6) of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008.

citations.text: The audit team noted that the tool used by CBs has limited possibilities. CBs have to indicate whether parcels, chosen from a dropdown list, are compliant or not with the organic requirements. However, CBs cannot and do not report on non-compliances other than those affecting the organic status of products. In addition, not all parcels subject to controls can be reported as only the parcels receiving subsidies are in the system. As a result, several non-compliances and the risk thereof are not reported to the NPA. Moreover, non-compliances detected after 30th October of a given year can only be notified if the parcel receives subsidies during the following year. CBs also stated that irregularities concerning animal husbandry may not be notified as they cannot be linked to parcels in the system.

The audit team was informed that the NPA had deducted payments to six farmers in 2014 following the notification of results from CBs. However, this figure is much smaller than the total number of irregularities affecting the organic status of the product which were notified by CBs in their annual reports submitted to the CU. This indicates that results notified to the CU may differ from the results notified to the NPA. The CU does not directly notify the results to the NPA, and only the CBs do so. Therefore, the system in place in Bulgaria used by the CBs does not fully ensure that information on the results of inspections and visits is communicated to the NPA, contrary to Article 92 (6) of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008. International Accreditation Forum (IAF) decision, the implementation of the new standard was subject to a three-year transition period expiring in September 2015. 5 Conclusions on Competent Authorities, Control Authorities and Control Bodies

The system in place in Bulgaria does not fully ensure that information on the results of inspections and visits is communicated to the NPA. 5.2.1.1 Control Bodies: Approval, Supervision and Withdrawal Legal Requirements Article 5(2) and (3) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 Article 27(5) to (9) and (14) of Regulation (EC) No 834/2007 Article 92c of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008 Findings

recommendations.text: Ensure that annual supervision takes into account the reports issued by Accreditation Bodies on all CBs operating in Bulgaria, as established by Article 92c(1) of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008, and that the supervision is adequate to verify the effectiveness of controls carried out by CBs, as required by Article 27(9)(b) of Regulation (EC) No 834/2007.

citations.text: However, although accreditation is a compulsory requirement for approval, the CU does not take into account the accreditation reports issued by Accreditation Bodies when carrying out the annual supervision to CBs, which is not in line with Article 92c(1) of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008. At the time of the audit, the CU had not requested any accreditation reports on the seven CBs whose headquarters are based in other MSs, nor 6 had the CU established cooperation arrangements for supervision with the CAs of those MSs. The CU requested the IABSA to provide, but had not received to date the reports on the four CBs whose headquarters are in Bulgaria (see paragraph 9).

However, the systematic shortcomings observed by the audit team, described in several sections of this report, were not noted by the CU, inter alia: CBs do not appear to have the infrastructure required and sufficient staff to adequately carry out their tasks. Timing and preparation of inspections are often not adequate Documented procedures used by CBs were very basic and checklists did not contain all relevant requirements or criteria to be checked during inspections; Risk analysis applied by both CBs did not serve as an adequate basis to determine the nature and frequency of visits; CB2 did not carry out adequate annual inspections to subcontracted operators. CB2 did not carry out any additional visits based on risk and the selection of operators for sampling was not risk-based in the majority of the cases. CBs did not immediately notify major non-compliances affecting the organic status of products, neither to the CU nor to other CBs. Such notifications take place with a great delay. Sampling procedures were not always adequate to ensure the reliability of the samples, and they were not always followed by inspectors; Inspectors systematically overlooked relevant requirements during the inspections. 7

The CU does not adequately assess the information received from CBs in their annual reports. For example, CB1 reported in 2014 that 26 samples tested positive for the presence of unauthorised PPPs, while CB2 reported no positive results. The audit team noted that 60% of the samples were taken by CB2 from the same product, and in most cases, not at operators with high risk profiles. Moreover, CB1 notified in the 2015 annual report a total number of irregularities three times higher than the number notified by CB2, which had not reported any major irregularities in at least the last three years. This obvious difference between the results of controls did not provoke any reaction from the CU.

Annual supervision is carried out by the CU on the delegated CBs. However, it is not adequate to verify the effectiveness of controls as it failed to identify and address the systematic severe shortcomings in the performance of the CBs.
Reports issued by Accreditation Bodies are not taken into account when the CU carries out supervision of CBs.

recommendations.text: Ensure that when systematic or severe shortcomings on the performance of CBs are found, effective corrective measures are taken, including the withdrawal of the approval when such bodies are failing to carry out properly the tasks delegated to them, as required by Article 27(9)(d) of Regulation (EC) No 834/2007.

citations.text: The CU is responsible for the approval and withdrawal of CBs. Accreditation by an Accreditation Body is a prerequisite to obtain and maintain approval. CBs must be accredited to ISO/IEC 17065:2012. The validity of approval matches the period of validity of accreditation, and it is only extended by the CU if accreditation is renewed by the AB. The accreditation of two CBs to EN 45011 expired on 30 Sept 2014 and the CU extended the validity of the approval as the IABSA had also extended the validity of their accreditation to EN 45011 until 30 March 2015. The IABSA carried out an accreditation audit to both CBs in August 2014 and at the time of the audit, all four CBs were accredited in Bulgaria to ISO 17065. Approval shall be withdrawn if CBs are no longer accredited or if they cease to fulfil their obligations, in line with Article 27 (9) of Regulation (EC) No 834/2007. However, fines or any measures other than withdrawal of the approval are not foreseen, which in practice makes it difficult for the CU to impose effective measures on the CBs to correct any shortcoming detected during supervision.

The CU supervises the execution of delegated controls carried out by CBs. Supervision is carried out annually, covering all areas of the CBs activity, in line with EU provisions. Office audits with a duration of two-three days are carried out at the headquarters of the CBs. Documented procedures are checked as well as at least 1% of operator´s files. The CU also checks the background, training of inspectors and the absence of any conflict of interest. In addition, witness audits are carried out during two-three days to observe the performance of inspectors. When non-compliances are found, they are reported to the CB as well as deadlines for the CBs to implement corrective action. The audit team checked a number of supervision reports and noted that the CU had reported no shortcomings in 2014 as regards CB1 and only two and one shortcoming in 2015 as regards CB1 and CB2 respectively. The audit team noted that CB2 repeated the same shortcoming during the annual inspection carried out three months after the supervision had taken place, meaning that the CB was not implementing the adequate corrective action to remedy the situation.

Even when shortcomings are found in the performance of CBs, no effective corrective measures are in place to rectify the situation, as only withdrawal of approval, while foreseen, is not applied in practice, and other measures are not set out 5.2.2 Registration of Operators Legal Requirements Article 28(1), (2) and (5) of Council Regulation (EC) No 834/2007 Article 92(2) and 92b of Commission Regulation (EC) No 889/2008 Findings

recommendations.text: Ensure that the list of registered operators is adequately updated to reflect changes in the organic status of the operators as required by Article 37(5) of the National Regulation, and that such list contains updated documentary evidence for all operators, as required by Article 92(b) of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008.

citations.text: The CU is responsible for maintaining the list of operators subject to the control system, which is publicly available since 2012. Applications submitted by operators to notify 2 In their response to the draft report, the CA noted that "An amendment to the ZPOOPZPES was initiated by Order No RD-09-225 of 2 April 2015. The amended law was promulgated in the State Gazette (SG) No 19 of 11 March 2016 and will enter into force on 1 April 2016. The amended ZPOOPZPES introduces additional sanctions, which the CU may impose on CBs. The additional sanctions (including financial) are stipulated in Articles 22(3) and (4) and 64(3) of the ZPOOPZPES." 8 their activities are uploaded onto the list by the CU. The information on new operators subject to the control system is supplemented by CBs, who must also update any relevant changes affecting the organic status of the operators under their control. According to the National Regulation, the deadline for CBs to upload any such change is three days. However, the audit team noted several cases where this deadline was not met, which is not in line with Article 37(5) of the National Regulation. In addition, CBs do not alert the CU in case that they find any contradictory information on the list.

The audit team checked the list and noted that it shows the name and location of the operators, the CB controlling their activities and the organic status (organic or in conversion to organic production). The date when operators sign a contract is established as the starting date for the conversion period. The list may also include as an attachment the documentary evidence issued by CBs as well as Annexes with details on products and quantities certified, suppliers and clients. All relevant changes in the status of operators are kept in the system and can be easily tracked. However, at the time of the DG Health and Food Safety audit, documentary evidences were only available for a limited number of operators, not fulfilling the requirement of Article 92(b) of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008.

The CU publishes a list of registered operators and is responsible to keep it updated. The 9 lists keeps track all of relevant changes in the status of operators since the time of registration. However, the list does not include all updated documentary evidence and it is not always adequately updated in order to reflect changes in the organic status of operators.

recommendations.text: Ensure that adequate communication is exchanged between CBs when operators and/or subcontractors move CB, and in particular that: The operators´ control files and the reports referred to in the second subparagraph of Article 63(2) of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008 are transferred in all cases from the previous CB to the subsequent CB to which the operators move to, as required by Article 92(2) of the same Regulation; 31 The change is adequately notified without delay to the Competent Authority by the CBs concerned, as required by Article 92(2) of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008.

citations.text: When operators move CB, the relevant elements of the operators´ file and the reports referred to in the second subparagraph of Article 63(2) must be transferred from the previous CB to the subsequent CB. However, the audit team noted several cases where this relevant information was not transferred. This is not in line with Article 92 of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008. The change must also be notified to the CU by the CBs concerned. The CBs do not notify directly to the CU but by uploading the information on the operators onto the list instead. This approach was proved to be inadequate as the CU was unaware of the change. The audit team noted several cases when operators had signed a contract with a new CB without informing the original CB. As a result, the operator was officially under the control of two CBs in parallel during several months without the original CB or the CU being aware of it, even if the new CB had uploaded this information onto the list. This may allow for situations where non-compliant products decertified by one CB may still be marketed by using documentary evidence issued by the other CB.

The exchange of communication between CBs is not always adequate when operators move CB, and it is not ensured that the operator´s control file and the reports referred to in Article 63(2) of Regulation (EC) No 889/2008 are transferred from the previous CB to the subsequent CB. In addition, the notification of the changes made by CBs to the CU is not adequate as it cannot be ensured that the CU is aware of such change having taken place.
